ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hotpot, Taskchain and Quizport
ResponsesInList.Text: 1. Does Taskchain for 2.3 exist yet? Is it still in the wind? TaskChain exists. It is not finished, but it is nearly finished. I am working on it as fast as I can. 2. If there is a Hoptpot mini moot next year in SF, does this mean HP is basically here to stay? As Mary has pointed out, the question implies some confusion about what "HP" is. The Hot Potatoes suite of programs that runs on a PC and allows teachers to create interactive web exercises is probably "here to stay", in the sense that the creators of the software, Martin Holmes and Stewart Arneil, have made it available on the website of their employers, University of Victoria (Canada), and it will probably remain there for the foreseeable future. Even if it disappears from there, you will probably be able to get a copy fron one of the web archiving sites that exist. The HotPot module for Moodle 1.x and the HotPot module for Moodle 2.x are "here to stay" for as long as Moodle 1.x and 2.x exist. What will happen when Moodle 3.x comes along? Well, that depends on a lot of things, but if I am still around and still willing and able to maintain the software, then I will do so - probably. The occasion of the HotPot mini-Moot in SF, means simply that there is a HotPot mini-Moot in SF. I will be there and hope many other users fo the software will be there, so that we can meet and talk and give each other ideas. It is a time for members of an online community to meet face-to-face. My only hidden agenda is to enjoy it 3. Why is HP simulaneously NOT open source and NOT being developed. Is this a big risk? As I understand it, the Hot Potatoes software (which as Mary pointed out I did not create) is not open source because (a) it was developed with funding from the University of Victoria and so would need their permission to make open source, and that would require the intervention of the University's lawyers which complicates matters, and (b) Martin and Stewart don't have time to develop it any further. AS it is they still spend a lot of time supporting the Hot Potatoes community by responding to questions on the Yahoo Hot Potatoes Users group. I don't see it as a big risk, because as I mentioned in my answer to question (1), I would think that you could get a copy of the Hot Potatoes download from now until the end of internet time. 4. Personal opinion (shoot me down in flames if you like): the output files I say yesterday from Hotpot seem to look so old fashioned, 1990's like. I presume you can fix this with CSS. But the content was great. Fair enough, but then again it is not surprizing that the native Hot Potatoes output formats look like they were designed in the 90's because they were. For me, the "genius" aspect of the Hot Potatoes suite is that it provides such an accessible and intuitive way to create XML files for quizzes. Once you have the XML files, you can feed them to an output generation engine and produce any output format you like. That is what QuizPort and TaskChain are designed to do. The provide a framework by which any XML file (or other data format for that matter) can be read in and converted to potentially *any* output format. I was not able to do it for QuizPort, but for TaskChain I hope I will be able to create more output formats, such as Flash, AJAX and HTML5 formats that look a spiffy and whizzo as you can imagine. You won't need to modify your input files, you just select a different output format. It is a very powerful notion - a threshold concept if you like - and it is the main reason why I continue to believe that these modules have a future. They provide a platform for owners / creators of *any* quiz format to administer elearning content via Moodle, without the need to create a Moodle module and worry about having to update it all the time as Moodle continues its unstoppable development cycle at breakkneck speed. 5. I know what it is like: you get by with what you have got, and don't develop the new thing. Is this what has happened to Taskchain? Actually, this is not my philosophy. I am something of an idealist. I want my software to be as good as it can be. As Glenys pointed out, I would prefer to answer *all* your questions, than answer just a few. My programming and software development style is the same. I am meticulous, and the end result is software that stands the test of time. It is rugged and tough, yet flexible and adapts to the user. It is industrial strength and ready for production. 6. I've read this "Lesson compared to Quizport" thread: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=140319 Is Quizport a commercial product in some way (having to buy licenses?) The free version of QuizPort does not include the backup and restore scripts, but is otherwise unrestricted. I will send you the backup and restore scripts if you send me a license fee: US $50 for a single teacher license, US $300 for an institutional license, The institutional license allows all teachers on a single Moodle site or at a single physical educational institution to use the software. If you cannot afford the license or believe you should not have to pay because you have contributed to the software in some way, please contact me privately (gordon at-sign kanazawa hyphen gu dot ac dot jp). TaskChain will be slightly different. The free version will include backup and restore (for Moodle 2.x) A number of commercial add-ons will be available, including modern output formats, a variety of media players, conversion of QuizPort (Moodle 1.9) activities, and various functionality improvements. 7. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hotpot, Taskchain and Quizport
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Derek, Let me join in by saying a few things. Hot Potatoes 'look old-fashoined' but you're right to say by using CSS you can give them a modern 'look'. Their look has little to do with how they function, though. And it's the content that matters. HotPotatoes are very granular and you can style them through CSS as you like (CSS3 especially can give them a really modern 'outfit'). Another thing, as I see it, is how the web evolves. Mobile! I've been getting numerous requests for mobile content recently. And as there is an increasing demand for mobile content delivered for Tablets and iPads, HotPotatoes does a good job too. HTML5 will give Hotpotatoes 5-10 more years of life. We've had several discussions on the HotPotatoes support yahoogroup and I've already ported my source files to XHTML5. It's easy to do; but since HTML5 is still in development, nobody can say how things will turn out in the end when HTML5 becomes a W3C Recommendation (some time in 2014). And be absolutely W3C compliant. There was some trouble with validating Dubling Core metadata in HTML5, but that has been solved too (for now). We don't know how things will develop with Dublin Core and XHTML5 either. Anyway, so far XHTML5 has been very promissing. Martin and Stuart seem willing to release an XHTML5 version (that will be available alongside the current one). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using Hot Potatoes for Quizzes
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ryan, I think there's maybe a bit of a vocabulary problem. In ordinary English "quiz" and "test" are often used interchangeably. Here I'll use "test" to mean "assess a student's knowledge". "Quiz" is a native Moodle module/activity which creates various interactive quizzes (QCMs, gap fill, etc.) and is primarily designed to make tests but can also be used for learning exercises. "Hot Potatoes" is an non-native module/activity which also creates various interactive quizzes (QCMs, gap fill, etc.) but they're primarily designed to be learning exercises (students get helpful feedback and can explore until they find the right answer). One of the exercise types in in Hot Potatoes is called JQuiz - it produces mainly MCQs . Hot Potatoes exercises can be uploaded and integrated into Moodle in 4 different ways : As HTML pages: the scores are not recorded in the Moodle gradebook. Through the Hot Potatoes Module (exists for Moodle 1.9 - has to be turned on by the admin & Moodle 2 - has to be added as a plugin). The scores are recorded in the Moodle gradebook. Through the QuizPort Module (exists only for Moodle 1.9 - has to be added as a plugin). This has more sophisticated ways of presenting the exercises and guiding the student through sequences of exercises. The scores are recorded in the Moodle gradebook. They can be imported into the Quiz module where they appear to the student just like other questions created in Quiz itself. Hope that helps, Glenys

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hotpot pictures in 2.2.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Erin, make sure the picture is in the same folder as the JCloze file. In the JCloze quiz, make sure that the picture is specified using only the name of the picture file, e.g. mypicture.jpg. If the picture is specified using a long name that includes folders, such as "C://My Documents/images/mypicture.jpg" then it will not work when you upload it to Moodle. Once you have check that the picture is specified in JCloze using just the picture file name, then generated the JCloze web file, the html file, and view it in your browser. Check that you can see the picture. Now login to Moodle and go to your course and add a new HotPot activity. Click on the "Add" button for the "Source file" and upload the JCloze "jcl" file (not the html file), and the picture file too. Now save changes and confirm that you can see the the HotPot quiz and it displays the image correctly. best regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Storage of HotPot Scores in database
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I am having a few problems with the way HotPot stores scores in the database . I am using a html file with my HotPot content - the user can check their answers as many times as they want until they have them all correct. I would like to store the score from the first time they check the answers. It seems that the data is stored to the database when the user navigates away from the page and that the code that deals with the submission of the score is handled by some of the other files in the module. Unfortunately they seem to submit the number of correct answers at the time when the user navigates away from the page. Which files handle this? I have looked but been unable to figure out what to hack. Another problem is that the score that is saved in the attempt is turned into a percentage - I would prefer to keep it as a simple total. Again I have searched for the code that does this, but have been unable to locate it. Any suggestions? Best wishes, Pete

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Storage of HotPot Scores in database
ResponsesInList.Text: Pete, what you are trying to do is not easy because it is not the way that Hot Poaatoes exercises work naturally. It would require modifying several parts of the HotPot module. You would need to modify the JavaScript that sends the results, the PHP which receives those results, and the PHP which displays the reports. In Moodle 1.x, the HotPot module had a "click trail" report, which if enabled would store and display information (inculding the score and state of each question) at every click of a button as the student did the quiz. However, I have not yet implemented that report on the HotPot module for Moodle 2.x) because I did not feel that many people used it, and I was more focussed on the TaskChain module which will be the successor to the HotPot module. regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Storage of HotPot Scores in database
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gordon, Yes, that is pretty much what I was thinking. However, this is what I need the scripts to do - scoring after the user has had as many attempts as they want is not very useful, especially if the answer is just a letter or number Similarly, percentages are not that helpful, especially if several exercises are being combined to make a single task. Of course, I could convert the percentages back to raw numbers but this seems a rather clumsy way of doing it. So my question is this. Given that I am uploading a JCloze task in html, which files do I need to modify? Cheers, Pete

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Storage of HotPot Scores in database
ResponsesInList.Text: Pete, I suggest you start by modifying the javascript functions in your html file so that they calculate a score that you feel is useful. For JCloze the main function that calculates the score is called "CheckAnswers". Change the function as little as possible, because the HotPot module will also try some search-and-replace transformations on that function. good luck! Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Storage of HotPot Scores in database
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gordon, Yes, I already have modified the js in my html file so that it checks the answers and calculates the scores that I want. The issue is that when the score is stored in the database it is done by a function somewhere in the hotpot mod - this does not produce the results I want as it stores the final score, not the initial score. All I need is a pointer to the files that handle the storage of the score in the db. I can then see how to go about amending the code. Cheers, Pete

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Storage of HotPot Scores in database
ResponsesInList.Text: > it stores the final score, not the initial score. So change your javascript so that it sends the initial score as the final score - then you will get what you want, without chainging any of the server -side scripts. > All I need is a pointer to the files that handle the storage of the score in the db In the "mod/hotpot/storage.php" script, have a look at the "store()" function (around line 63). all the best Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Storage of HotPot Scores in database
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gordon, I'm still grappling with this. I've got much of it working in the way that I want, but still having problems in key areas. First of all, changing the javascript  so that it sends the initial score rather than the final score does not work. I used: if(firstattempt==0){Score = TotalScore;} firstattempt++; This works fine when used in isolation, but when the file is uploaded to Moodle it seems to be overridden. I suspect that the function that stores the score in the database fetches the score by using a script in the mod. Similarly, I am completely unable to find the code that coverts the score to a percentage. I have got round this by simply writing some code that coverts it back to a score, but this seems rather silly and also it's a nuisance because I need to pass the the total number of questions each time. It would make more sense to change the code so that it stores the actual score. It seems to me that both of these are things that could usefully be available as options. Many people who want to use hotpot as a learning tool are likely to be interested in how many items the learner gets correct first time, rather than how many they can get correct after an infinite number of clicks. Similarly, raw scores may be more interesting than percentages, especially if learners are working on multiple activities which may have different totals. Best wishes, Pete

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Storage of HotPot Scores in database
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Pete, the function that calculates and stores the score to send back to Moodle is in an external javascript file: mod/hotpot/attempt/hp/6/jquiz/jquiz.js If you look in there for the "setScoreAndPenalties()" function, you could experiment with changing that so it works how you want it to. Having changed that file, you will of course need to empty your browser's cache so that the browser fetches the new js file from the server. In my opinion the scoring of HotPot and other kinds of quiz is too complicated to be whilttled down to "options". I believe a more flexible and robust solution is to create a new "output format". So for example, in your case, once you have a working prototype, you can create a new output format for JQuiz and then in the future select that everytime you want to use that on a JQuiz on your Moodle site. If enough people agree with you that the "raw score"  and number of corretc first time is important info to have, then we can considier adding the new JQuiz output format to the HotPot module at some point in the future, once you have it working. best regards Gordon

(hbs stands for HalfBaked Software, and this is the original player developed by Martin and Stewart) The other hbs versions by Bernard Dyer and Birgit Ferran with the sliders are based on this player. ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Christina, I'm guessing you don't have the right path.  My way of finding the path to the mp3 is: Through HotPot I upload the swf and the exercise files. Then I "Save and display". When the exercise loads, I go to "View source" and find out the path to the swf. Since the sfw and the mp3s are in the same place, I then edit the exercise and put the absolute path. For instance, I have this for the swf player: <param name="src" value=" http://www.e-learnlanguage.eu/moodle/pluginfile.php/241/mod_hotpot/sourcefile/ hbs_mp3_player.swf" /> I copy the path up to the player ( http://www.e-learnlanguage.eu/moodle/pluginfile.php/241/mod_hotpot/sourcefile/ ) and put it in <param name="FlashVars" value="TheSound=Clip1.mp3" /> to look like this <param name="FlashVars" value="TheSound= http://www.e-learnlanguage.eu/moodle/pluginfile.php/241/mod_hotpot/sourcefile/ Clip1.mp3" /> Re-upload the exercise overwriting the previous upload and .... it works for me. Cheers Stan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Images not displaying in JQuiz
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Hary, Although the folder is in the root, the problem is that Moodle is unaware that hese images are there. Potentially in the future: when you upgrade Moodle, this folder may disappear. Another risk is that there will be all sorts of images and you have to develop a consistent naming convention for them to be able to manage them. There's also the risk of overwriting the files if other people also upload files there. Imagine the scenario where two people have named an image hat.png and it appears in several courses and your course displays somebody else's hat.png image in different size, etc. On the other hand, that's what Moodle is - a Content management system and since Moodle is unaware of the images folder, you cannot manipulate it from within Moodle, you cannot manupulate the image files from wihtin Moodle - you always have to do it through FTP . All users with the respective rights can upload images to their courses. In your case, how many people will have access to FTP to upload images? And if I were the Admin, I wouldn't like to be responsible for dealing with everyone's image uploads all the time, especially when people are testing their exercises. Now it's images, next comes audio and then video and you may end up with a completely new file system. As a CMS, Moodle takes care of rewriting the relative paths to absolute paths, and so does HotPot (and other modules). If the https is the problem, then Gordon already solved it. I'm sorry if I'm explaining something very basic but this must be your last resort; there must be other ways. I believe not all options are exhausted. Cheers Stan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HotPot record is missing sourcetype
ResponsesInList.Text: Manga, we are getting a little confused because we are using the word "import" differently. There are two ways to administer a Hot Potatoes quiz via Moodle: create a HotPot activity and use the Hot potatose file as the "Source file" for the HotPot activity go to the Moodle question bank, click the "Import" link, select "Hot Potatoes XML file", upload the Hot Potatoes file, and click the "import" button. The question(s) can now be added to a Moodle Quiz activity It seems that you use "import" to talk about both situations. However, when I say "import" I mean only case number (2) above. I do not use "import" to talk about case (1). Instead, I use a phrase such as "add a HotPot activity". If the permissions are not allowing the web server to read the PHP scripts, then you will not be able to add a HotPot activity or import a Hot Potatoes file into the question bank. Once you have verified that the permissions are correct, please try the "import" again and let us know how you get on. regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HotPot record is missing sourcetype
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Manga, thanks for sending the access info to your server. I was able to login and have a good look around. If you move up to Moodle 2.3, you will need at least 256 MB. Moodle 2.2: requirements Moodle 2.3: requirements Overall, I would say you server is underpowered for Moodle 2.x, and I recommend you move to different server, or upgrade your current server, so that it can run more comfortably. if it is struggling now, with only you and me on it, I suspect it will grind to a halt when the students start hitting it. In my experience, Windows servers are more sluggish than the Linux counterparts, so unless you have a strong reason to stick with Windows, I suggest you switch to a Linux host , that has lots of memory. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HotPot > Access Control > Previous Activity. Also Next Activity mdl2.2
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jeff, thanks for pointing out the issues with the help text for previous and next activities . I have fixed those in the HotPot English language pack. Regarding the behavior of previous and next activity for a "teacher" (or equivalent role on your Moodle site), I understand that you wish to experience what the students experience, but the difficulty is that if the teacher was barred from viewing a HotPot because they had not achieved the required grade on a previous activity, they would never be able to get into the HotPOt to view the reports or change settings. Similarly, I think we want to give the teacher the option of whether to stay with this HotPot or choosing to continue after they finish a HotPot in case they want to change settings or view repotrs. At least that is how I usually work. So for now I would ilke to leave it that the teacher needs to switch to the student role for the previous and next activty functionality to kick in. You can change role directly from the HotPot page using "Setting" menu (see attached screenshot) To tell the truth, the previous and next activity settings may not be necessary in Moodle 2.x, because to some extent they duplicate the "Conditional activities" functionality of Moodle 2.x. As you know the "M" in Moodle is for modular, and being a modular piece of software the various components are not supposed to interfere with each other's settings or access them directly. They should only access them via an established interface, called an API. For this reason, an activity module such as the HotPot module is not supposed to unilaterally grey out items on the course page, and similarly I do not think there is a way for the course page to tell the HotPot module what it's conditional completion conditions are, so we can't use that information to display the exit page or go immediately to a specfied activity. At the moment, I think we will leave the previous and next activity settings in HotPot and wait to see if they are really necessary in Modle 2.x. I hope that answers your questions, but if not please let me know. chesrs Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: decimal sums in hotpot
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Can anyone advise how I can give more than one answer to simple sums using decimals EG the answers 0.7 or .7 or 0.700 or 0.7000 etc are all correct. I am creating question in Hotpotatoes and then importing them into the question bank in moodle. Thanks in advance. Stephen

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: decimal sums in hotpot
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stephen, in Hot Potatoes JQuiz you can give more than one predicted answer and then specify the score for each answer. If you make the score for all your predicted answers 100%, then any of them will be judged to be a correct answer ... I think. It doesn't quite capture the essence of the issue that I think you are trying to solve which is to ignore trailing zeros, or more generally to  use only a certain number of significant decimal places, or maybe even accept any answer within a given range. I believe the numeric question type in the Moodle question bank can handle those concepts more elegantly, but unfortunately there is no corresponding editor in Hot Potatoes, so you would have to import them using a different format, e.g. GIFT. The Hot Potatoes programs are more suitable for text-based exercises. Here are some help docs: Moodle question types: Numerical question type Moodle question import: GIFT import format (numerical questions) regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quiz Port question
ResponsesInList.Text: Bohdana, I think you are looking at the wrong page. I think you are looking at the QuizPort activity settings page, but you should be looking at the QuizPort *quiz* settings page. There is no "Delay 3" setting on the page for editing a QuizPort activity. That page has the title that begins with "Updating QuizPort". The "Delay "3 setting is on the settings page for each quiz within a QuizPort activity. Each quiz within a QuizPort activity has its own settings page. You can get to a QuizPort quiz's settings page by clicking the edit icon, , next to the title when you are viewing the QuizPort quiz. The title at the top of a QuizPort quiz's settings page says "Updating: Quiz". That page has a "Delay 3" setting on it. If you can't see it there, you need to click the "Show advanced" button within the "Access control" section of the page. HTH Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quiz Port question
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bohdana > maybe it's possible to change all of them (=the > Delay 3 settings on all quizzes in all QuizPorts) > at the same time using one model and filter? Yes, you can do this as follows go to the "Edit quizzes" page for any of your QuizPort activities select "Access control" from the "Show columns" drop-down menu if necessary, edit one of the quizzes to make sure its "Delay 3" setting is set to the value you want to apply to all the other QuizPort quizzes on the "Edit Quizz" page, select the checkbox at the top of the "Delay 3" column in the "Default" column, select a quiz with the desired "Delay 3" setting at the bottom of the page, select " Apply selected default values ", and then select " Quizzes matching the following filters " click the "Go" button OK, you've done it. All the quizzes in all the QuizPorts in that course now use the new "Delay 3" setting. Note that if you want to apply this setting to all quizzes in all QuizPort in the whole site , you can do that too. The instructions are the same as above, except that after step 6, you select "All" from the "Course" filter. The resume button on the entry page for a QuizPort will allow students to resume their work from where they left off last time. For example, if they stopped halfway through quiz 4 in a unit of 8 quizzes, then the resume buton will let them resume from quiz 4 without having to redo quizzes 1, 2 and 3. If you want to let them attempt the quizzes any number of times, then set the "Attempts allowed" setting to "Unlimited attempts" on both the QuizPort activity settings page and each quiz's settings pages. If you want to force students to do the quizzes in order the first time, but once they have done completed the activity give them free, unfettered access to the quizzes, then set the QuizPort activity's "Allow free access" setting to something other than "No". more info: Allow free access enjoy! Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hot Potatoes, Quiz, QuizPort, Xerte...?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Deborah, yes, it is possible to do what you want to do, but you will have to work very hard to get it. First, let us remember that from QuizPort's point of view, your Xerte exercise is a single thing with a single status, score and xml-encoded results. If you send the results back to QuizPort with the status set to "1" (= in progress), then I don't think QuizPort will try to move on to something else. We can put what we like into the xml, so you could certainly put all the information you want about which "pages" in your Xerte have been attempted, and what the details of the interaction with each page were. However, we would also need a PHP script sitting in the right place in QuizPort, so that we could then extract those details from the XML and present them to the teacher and student in a readable format. Now, QuizPort knows all about how the results from Hot Potatoes quizzes are encoded in XML, so one possible shortcut you could consider is to encode your Xerte results in the same way as a Hot Potatoes quiz does. I would think a JQuiz would be the most suitable place to start. Here is a document I made to help me remember the format of the XML of Hot Potatoes quizzes: http://bateson.kanazawa-gu.ac.jp/moodle/19/mysql/mod/quizport/docs/developer/21.xml.doc It probably doesn't make much sense at first glance, but if you couple that with looking at some actual examples of your Hot Potatoes quizzes in action, you may begin to get the idea of how it all works. You can see the actual XML that is used by Hot Potatoes quizzes within QuizPorts on your site if you first enable Site Administration -> Modules -> Activities -> QuizPort -> Store the raw XML details of QuizPort quiz attempts, and then attempt a simple JQuiz administered via QuizPort. The results will be stored in the mdl_quizport_details table in your database (in the "details" field). It may be possible to utilize the javascript functions and classes the QuizPort uses to encode the results as XML. Those are located in the "mod/quizport/output/hp/hp.js" file on your Moodle site. For example, here is the URL for that file on my server: http://bateson.kanazawa-gu.ac.jp/moodle/19/mysql/mod/quizport/output/hp/hp.js This may be all rather more technical that you would have liked, but there we are, that's the way it is. That is the unbridled, beautiful truth of how it all works. best regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Installing Hot Potatoes in Moodle 2.2
ResponsesInList.Text: IF you do not have this file "mod/hotpot/lang/en/hotpot.php" then you have put the hotpot scripts in the wrong place, and the hotpot module is not yet installed on your site. You need to put the "hotpot" folder containing the hotpot module into the folder called "mod" under the main the folder containing the Moodle scripts. Also, in the "mod" folder are the folders for the other activity modules, such as "assignment", "forum" and "quiz". Can you find that folder? Put the "hotpot" folder there, and make the owner and permissions the same as the folders for the other activity modules. When you set the owner and permissions, make sure you set them recursively, using the "-r" switch, so that permissions on all the files within the "hotpot" folder are also set correctly. Once you are sure that "hotpot" folder is in the right place, try accessing the hotpot readme file. If your webserver (probably Apache) can read that, then the permissions are probably correct. The url of the readme file is something like this: http://localhost/moodle/mod/hotpot/readme.txt Can your browser display that? If you can't, go back and fix the path, owner or permissions of the hotpot module script. If you can view the readme.tt file, you are ready to install the module. To install the module, login to Moodle as the main administrator and click on Settings -> Site administration -> Notifications.

ResponsesInList.Title: QuizPort reset
ResponsesInList.Text: Calling all QuizPort teachers and admins, I have noticed noticed some strangeness about QuizPort activities that had been reset as part of a course reset. It turns out there was a bug in the QuizPort reset script. The bug manifests in two ways: although the QuizPort grades were all reset, if a student who had been enrolled before the reset, came back to the course, they would find that on starting a QuizPort activity their results for individual quizzes within the QuizPort from before the reset were still there the following QuizPort tables did not reduce in size after a course reset: quizport_quiz_scores quizport_quiz_attempts I have fixed the bug and also modified the QuizPort upgrade script to remove all the orphaned records in the affected QuizPort tables in the Moodle database . The next time you upgrade QuizPort, and I encourage you to do so at your earliest convenience, all the orphaned records will be removed. If there are a lot of records, the upgrade will take some time, but it will eventually complete - even if your browser or server times out and you need to restart the upgrade. You can get the latest version of QuizPort from the Moodle plugins repository: QuizPort module for Moodle 1.x best regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Missing data type in hotpot dataset
ResponsesInList.Text: It may be enough to set the sourcetype manually using your favorite database administration tool (e.g. phpMyAdmin ) Assuming the prefix on your Moodle tables is "mdl_" (i.e. the default value), then the following SQL statements should set the sourcetype for files which have ".xml" added to the standard Hot Potatoes file extensions: UPDATE mdl_hotpot SET sourcetype='hp_6_jcloze_xml' WHERE sourcefile LIKE '%.jcl.xml'; UPDATE mdl_hotpot SET sourcetype='hp_6_jcross_xml' WHERE sourcefile LIKE '%.jcw.xml'; UPDATE mdl_hotpot SET sourcetype='hp_6_jmatch_xml' WHERE sourcefile LIKE '%.jmt.xml'; UPDATE mdl_hotpot SET sourcetype='hp_6_jmix_xml' WHERE sourcefile LIKE '%.jmx.xml'; UPDATE mdl_hotpot SET sourcetype='hp_6_jquiz_xml' WHERE sourcefile LIKE '%.jqz.xml'; When you add new HotPot activities from now on, I suggest you use the standard Hot Potatoes file endings to ensure that ensure HotPot module correctly identifies the file type. Please let me know if this solution works for you. regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Text: Tzvi, I wanted the jmt file because it has the Hebrew characters in it. I wanted real live items to investigate with. Real data is richer and more complex than stuff I can come up with. Anyway, may be that doesn't matter ... I made a Hebrew jmt file by copying and pasting from your HMTL file. Then I created a standard JMatch HTML. Then I made a few changes to get it sort of working in Moodle 2.x. Here are the three changes I made (to a standard JMatch HTML file): in the CardOverlap() function ... replace these lines : var smR=(this.GetR()<(OtherCard.GetR()+this.OverlapTolerance))? this.GetR(): (OtherCard.GetR()+this.OverlapTolerance); var lgL=(this.GetL()>OtherCard.GetL())? this.GetL(): OtherCard.GetL(); with the following lines : var smR=Math.min(this.GetR(), OtherCard.GetR()); var lgL=Math.max(this.GetL(), OtherCard.GetL() - this.OverlapTolerance); In the CardDockToR() function ... replace this line : this.SetL(OtherCard.GetR() + 5); with this line: this.SetL(OtherCard.GetL() - 5 - this.GetW()); in the StartUp() function locate this line : var WidthToSet = WidestRight-12; insert the following lines AFTER the above line : var TempColPos = LeftColPos; LeftColPos = RightColPos; RightColPos = TempColPos; The attached file contains the above modifications and should perform reasonably well in any Moodle. You may find that the attached file is not perfect. For example cards that are wrongly placed go to a slightly odd position when you click the "Check" button. Also, your probably want to align the Hebrew text in right in the box that contains them. However, it is a good start. If you wish *all* you JMatch exercises to behave in this way, I suggest you modify the Hot Potatoes source files on your PC, as I mentioned in my earlier post. regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Making question area Right instead of default Left
ResponsesInList.Text: Tzvi, > I have no clue what these numbers mean... can I still nag you? I think you are asking me to explain what the numbers mean. Well OK, I will try, but to really understand it, you would have to look through the JavaScript and follow the flow of the program. Anyway, here's what I understand those numbers to mean ... "pg" is a javascript object representing the drag area, that is to say the DIV element that contains the fixed and movable cards pg.Left is the number of pixels from the left hand side of the browser page to the left hand side of "pg". However, this property of "pg" only exists within Moodle, so to prevent errors ourside of Moodle I have added "|| 0" which means if there is no pg.Left property, then use "0" instead pg.W is the width of "pg" expressed as a number of pixels "Widest" is the width in pixels of the widest of the fixed cards "WidestRight" is the width in pixels of the widest of the dragable cards LeftColPos is the position in pixels of the left hand side of the fixed cards RightColPos is the position in pixels of the left hand side of the dragable cards So in plain(ish) English, those two formulae mean ... position the fixed cards so that the right side of the cards lines up with the right side of the drag area position the dragable cards far enough to the left of the fixed cards, so there is enough room between the cards to drag and drop one of the dragable cards Sorry if that doesn't mean much to you, but those are the terms in which I think cheers Gordon

I notice from your screenshot that you have not yet uncommented the lines to make the Hebrew cards the same width as the English cards, but you know how to do that now, right? To shunt the starting position of the English cards further to the left, you can increase the value of the "14" number we talked about earlier. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Video-formats in Moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Henny, as always, the sure-fire way to get media players to work in Hot Potatoes quizzes administered via Moodle is to use absolute URLs, i.e. URLs that begin with "http://" to specify the player and the media file. If you use relative URLs, then you have to hope QuizPort can find them and convert them to absolute URLs for you. QuizPort knows some common places to look for URLs, including in the parameters passed to some common media players, but if you are using a media player that QuizPort is not familiar with, then the URLs won't get converted and the audio/video won't play. The full list of media file types that QuizPort knows about is: avi,flv,mov,mpeg,mp3,mp3,ram,rpm,rm,swf,wmv If flv is not working for you, I would be grateful if you could upload a simple example exercise (with video file) to my server , so I can have a look: URL : http://bateson.kanazawa-gu.ac.jp/moodle/19/mysql/ Course: Cours Fullname 101 Username: guestteacher Password: quizportv09 We could probably add mp4 too, because that seems to be something that the Moodle mediaplugin filter can use. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Making it easy for guests to do Hot Potatoes exercises
ResponsesInList.Text: Glenys, I understand what you want to do, but I would like you to understand the consequences of allowing guests in. Some teachers want the HotPot module to stop students "cheating". They expect that a student should only allowed to be able to do one attempt at a time. If students could do two attempts simultaneously, they could open two separate browser windows, start two separate attempts, and use one to discover the correct answers, and the other to input the right answers. They could thus achieve a perfect score without the effort and knowledge that the teacher was trying to elicit. For this reason, the HotPot module does not allow simultaneous attempts . When a user starts a new attempt at a HotPot activity, all the previous "in progress" attempts at that activity by that user are set to "abandoned", and the new attempt is set to "in progress". If the HotPot module receives results for an attempt that is "abandoned", it will refuse to store the results and will instead display a message saying something like "That attempt is not in progress". There is another possible complication of allowing guest users in, if you also allow your site to be open to Google and other search engines. If the search engines are allowed in to Moodle, they will be logged in as the guest user. If they are looking at the course page or resources or assignment explanation pages there is no problem, because the content on those pages doesn't change. However, if we give the search engine access to a HotPot page there is a good chance that the content is different every time, so the search engine will think that the page has been updated and will come back again and again to get the "latest" version of the page. Search engines are relentless and will keep coming back. Your server will be have to work to serve up the pages to the search engines, and depending on how many HotPots you have and how powerful your server is, your server may get overwhelmed. This problem can be compounded if you let the guest user be a teacher in a HotPot/QuizPort activity, in order to give them access to the "Preview" button. Now the search engine has access to the report pages, which change each time a student attempts a quiz. Remember that if you have allowed the search engine to attempt the HotPot quiz as a guest user, then those attempts will appear on the report page. The search engine will be endlessly trying to access the HotPot quizzes and report pages, and your server will be frantically trying to keep up. I have seen this perfect storm in action, and it took the server down within hours. The problem then is that the HotPot module and QuizPort module are designed and built assuming no guest access. This allows them to ignore simultaneous attempts and rules out the possiblity of search engines making uncescessary and excessive access to quiz and report pages. We could argue that for small sites or sites wishing to showcase online materials that don't cause a search engine feeding frenzy the above objections to guest access do not matter. However, if we make any changes to allow "easy" guest access, we must realize that this could affect the very core method of how these modules work, and could lead to confusion among many teachers as to "why has my site gone down, when all I did was enable guest access to HotPots". From my point of view, I think the most complete answer to this issue is to change the login scripts in Moodle core to allow dynamically-assigned multiple and separate guest access. In such a system, when a user requests guest access, the system will check to see if any already created guest account is currently logged out. If such a guest account exists, the user will be logged in using that guest account. If no guest account is available, a new one is created. If the user was given a previously existing account then all previous Quiz and HotPot (and QuizPort) attempts are removed, so that the user starts their Moodle access with a clean slate. You can see such a system in action at the following site. You will notice that when you log in, you are given a user name such as "FNE Guest (3)", when the number in brackets indicates which guest user you are logged in as. Here is the URL : FearNoEnglish.com: Bucchake English Listening course In the interests of openness, I should say that the above site is run myself and a buddy. It is free to use. I am offering it here simply as an example ofmultiple separate guests on Moodle. You should be aware that the programming required for that feature required several months work (in 2009), and is not a task I would suggest you undertake without a lot of understanding of what is involved. regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Text: Glenys, looking at the "book" module backup and restore scripts, it seems they will detect and transfer absolute URLs from the old site to the new site: The old URLs should be one of the following: book's first chapter e.g. ht tp://www.oldsite.com/moodle/book/view.php?id=99 where "99" is a course module id of a book activity book's specific chapter e.g. ht tp://www.oldsite.com/moodle/book/view.php?id=99&chapterid=88 where "99" is a course module id of a book activity and "88" is an optional chapterid within the book book index page in a course e.g. ht tp://www.oldsite.com/moodle/book/index.php?id=99 where "99" is a course id, i.e. not a course module id If you put these links in the entry page text or exit page text of a QuizPort activity, they should be backed up and restored correctly. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 1.9 and importation of images from Hot Pot
ResponsesInList.Text: When you import a Hot Potatoes file to the question bank, the import script only has that one file to look at. If it finds a image specified with a relative URL , such as , it tries to convert the URL to an absolute URL but it has to guess where the image is. As I remember, the import script will first look to see if you are importing from the course "Files" folder, and if so it will fix the URL to point to where the image should be in there, relative to where the Hot Potatoes file is. However, if you are importing from a file that you uploaded straight into the import script, then there is no way of knowing where the image file will be Here are two workarounds which you may like to try: upload the Hot Potatoes file and its associated images to the course "Files" folder, and when you import use "Import from file already in course files" before you import, convert the image URLs to absolute URLs, i.e. something like "ht tp:/ /mys erver.com/images/declan.gif" Please let me know if either (or both!) of the above afford you a less tedious workflow than your current method. HTH Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Due date for hotpot exercises doesn´t show up in calendar in moodle 2.1.4+
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Luis, do I undersatnd correctly that the opening time was in the calendar, but the closing time was not? Maybe the " hotpot_maxeventlength " configuration setting is relevant here (Settings -> Site administration -> Plugins -> Activity modules -> HotPot -> Maximum number of days for a single calendar event) The default setting is 5 days. If the period between the open and close times are less than that, only one calendar event will be added. I think this is what happened in your case. Probably your fix is to reset the " hotpot_maxeventlength " setting to "1". Any HotPot activities that you create or edit after you have changed the setting and whose close date is more than one day after the open date, should create two calendar events. hope that helps! Gordon

Furthermore, when you change the site-wide " hotpot_maxeventlength " setting that I mentioned in my previous message, the HotPot module will check ALL the calendar events for ALL the HotPot activities on your Moodle site and adjust any that need to changed from a single event to two separate events and vice-versa. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Written assessment has to be 100% correct!!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Lori, I suggest you put all your questions, answers and feedback into a JQuiz exercise. You can enable the following setting within JQuiz if you want the questions shuffled into a different order each time they are displayed to the students: Options -> Configure Output -> Other -> Shuffle order of questions each time page loads You can add the JQuiz file to Moodle 1.9 using the HotPot module, but if you want a delay between attempts I suggest you use the QuizPort module. The QuizPort module is the successor to the HotPot module module, but it is not included in the standard download of Moodle 1.9, so you will have to downoad it and install it separately: QuizPort module for Moodle 1.x The QuizPort module allows you to put several Hot Potatoes exercises into a single QuizPort activity. You can add post-conditions to the exercises so that students can only finish the exercise if they get the required score - 100% in your case. The post-conditions would look something like this: >= 100%: end of unit same quiz In plain English this means, "If the score for the Hot Potatoes exercise is 100%, then this student has finished this QuizPort activity, otherwise show the same exercise again". On the settings page for the Hot Potatoes exercise within QuizPort you can specify delays between attempts at the exercise: delay1: the minimum delay between first and second attempts delay2: the minimum delay between attempts after the second attempt If you need help installing the QuizPort module, please let us know. cheers Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Student Feedback for a Hot Pot Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I am working on a project using Moodle 2.2. I like to give students the opportunity to provide feedback on activities they complete - this helps me improve the activities and gives me some idea of what problems students may be encountering. I have set up a feedback activity and I am wondering if there is any way to integrate this with the HotPot activity. I see that in HotPot there is a drop down list for "Student Feedback" but I haven't been able to find out anything about how these are used. One of the options from the drop down list is "Feedback Form" and I am wondering if this is something that I can use here. What are the other options and how do they work? Many thanks for input / advice. Best wishes and a happy new year to all, Pete

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Student Feedback for a Hot Pot Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Pete, the idea of the feedback form, is that information will be sent to a formmail type of script, which will receive the info and do something with it. Unless you are familiar with formmail, I wouldn't suggest you use this option. Instead, I suggest you try one of the other options. If you choose "Moodle forum" that will take students to the Moodle forum index, where they can choose a forum to send feedback and discuss the quiz they just took. If you have already setup a Feedback activity, you could copy the URL for that and paste it into the Student Feedback URL when the "Student feedback" for the HotPot is set to "Web page". THat you should give the effect I think you are aiming for. good luck! Gordon P.S. FYI , here is the help info for that option on that form (probably you have seen this already ... Student feedback If enabled, a link to a pop-up feedback window will be displayed whenever the student clicks on the "Check" button. The feedback window allows students to discuss this quiz with their teacher and classmates in one of the following ways: Web page requires URL of the web page, for example http://myserver.com/feedbackform.html Feedback form requires URL of the form script, for example http://myserver.com/cgi-bin/formmail.pl Moodle forum the forum index for the course will be displayed Moodle messaging the Moodle instant messaging window will be displayed. If the course has several teachers, the student will be prompted to select a teacher before the messaging window appears.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error installing quizport in moodel 2.1.1 spanish
ResponsesInList.Text: In Moodle 1.9 you can enter the folder name and the HotPot module will detect all HP quiz files within that folder and add a "Hot Potatoes Quiz" activity for each one. In Moodle 2.x, I'm afraid you have to create each HotPot activity individually when using the HotPot module. As reported on the following Moodle docs page, you can no longer add several HotPot activites at once: http://docs.moodle.org/22/en/HotPot_module_for_Moodle_2.0 Whether you use the HotPot module for Moodle 1.9 or 2.x, you will end up with 190 links on the course page. That's a lot of links and will be tough to navigate for both you and the students. If I were you I would use the QuizPort module for Moodle 1.9. It allows you to add several HP quizzes as a single unit, creating only one link on the course page. Furthermore, you can add pre- and post- conditions to the quizzes so that students can be guided on a certain path through the quizzes depending on their performance; good scores zoom ahead, poor scores go more slowly. The QuizPort module is available now, it has been around for a few years and I consider it to be a very stable piece of software. However it does not work on Moodle 2.x. The successor to the QuizPort module will be the TaskChain module. It will work on Moodle 2.x. It is currently in the final stages of creation, but it is not finished yet. I will be finished in the next few weeks. regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading problems
ResponsesInList.Text: I know what she did. She moved the top item, then pressed "check", then she moved the next item and then pressed "check", and so on. Every time she moved an item, she pressed check. The trouble is that every time she pressed "check" with some items not moved, the Hot Potatoes considers that the unmoved items are "wrong" and will reduce her score - slowly down to zero. You need to explain to her how to do these JMix quizzes: move all the items first, then PRESS "check" ONCE. Gordon

ResponsesInList.Text: Sarah, on re-reading this thread, I have realized that probably what is happening on your server is that *every* folder needs it's own php.ini file. The folders that were already there, such as the folder with the script that shows PHP info, function OK because they already have a php.ini, but the new folder, i.e. "mod/hotpot", does not have a php.ini. ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Robert, > INSERT INTO mdl_quizport_responses ( ATTEMPTID, ... ) VALUES ( 544519, ... ) Congratualtions to you and your students for doing over half a million attempts at QuizPort quizzes  - ! > INSERT INTO mdl_quizport_responses ( ATTEMPTID, ... CORRECT ) > VALUES ( 544519, ... '660,84,24411,2556,6524,283,337,1189,876,37260, > 177,3080,37242,2874,169,909,594,1009,8329,664,37261,874,342,18494, > 375,37262,180,3021,7560,648,341,50,221,37263,619,3059,347,22161, > 47,37264,5375,250,36076,178,698,36,3150,8947,37265,15807,37268, > 373,657,6,6531,1008,4977,1763,30,968,2704' ) What is happening here is that each word in the correct answer is assigned an id from the "strings" table and then this list of ids is stored in the "correct" field of the record in the "attempts" table. The "correct" field can be up to 256 chars long, but because the ids in your database are now large, combined with the fact that rhubarb quizzes require a lot of ids means that all those ids are now longer than the allowed length of the "correct" field. When we do the same activity on my server, the ids are all much shorter and therefore there is enough room for this information and we don't get the error on my server. I don't really want to make this field in the database longer, because at the moment the type of this field in the database is VARCHAR(256) whch is has a variable length and is quite an efficient way to store text fields that are usually short but sometimes long. To make the field longer, we would have to make it a fixed length TEXT field, but this would mean we have to allocate space for the field even if it is not used - and usually this field only contains a handful of ids. I think a better solution would be to rethink how to store Rhubarb results. For the moment, I will simply cut off the list of ids if it is going to be longer than 256 chars. This will mean that you lose some informationabout which words were entered. In the longer term I will implement a solution which allows the all the words to be stored. I will let you know when you can download a version of the QuizPort module which can handle your situation. best regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error installing Moodle with cPanel
ResponsesInList.Text: If have seen that error when PHP version is greater than 5.2.8 but less than 5.3. You need the PHP version to be greater than 5.2.8 to run early versions of Moodle 2.x, but there is some PHP syntax that is valid in PHP 5.3 that is not valid in PHP 5.2 The line that causes the error message is this: return $class::get_required_behaviours(); In order to work on PHP 5.2, the above line needs to be rewritten as ... return call_user_func(array($class, 'get_required_behaviours')); However, even if you fix the above line, there may be other simliar problems waiting down the line, so your best workaround is to upgrade to PHP 5.3.2 or later. By the way, if you want the HotPot module for Moodle 2.x you will have to install it yourself. You can get it from here: HotPot module for Moodle 2.x Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: audio-text glossing
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Robert, as is often the case when media players "don't work" in Moodle, the problem is the relative URLs. They need to be converted to absolute URLs. QuizPort knows where to look for some URLs, and it will convert any relative URLs that are in places that it knows about. However, in your file, "OWS-U05-001.htm", you need to change the relative URLs manually. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: deadlines disagreement
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Yolanda, I don't like to see you mad I would like to help you understand better about the "deadlines". Then I don't think you will be so mad. I think you understand that a QuizPort activity contains one or more quizzes. Each of the quizzes can have a "deadline", and also the QuizPort activity itself can have a "deadline". When the QuizPort software is deciding what to display to the student, it first checks the QuizPort activity "deadlines". If the QuizPort activity is not available, either because the open "deadline" has not yet arrived, or because the close "deadline" has already passed, the student will see a message saying: Sorry, this activity is not currently available to you. If the QuizPort activity is available to the student, then the QuizPort software will try to find a available quiz within the QuizPort activity. It will check the start and close "deadlines" for each quiz and try to find one that is available. If no quiz is available, the following message will appear: Sorry, this quiz is not currently available to you. Notice that the messages are slightly different. The first one is talking about "this activity", and the second one talks about "this quiz". Therefore by looking at the message you know whether is is caused by "deadlines" on the QuizPort activity, or on one of the quizzes within the QuizPort activity. OK, so how do we change deadlines? To change a "deadline" on a QuizPort activity , you log into Moodle as a teacher or admin and do one of the following: EITHER: switch the course page into edit mode, and click on the edit icon next to the QuizPort activity whose "deadlines" you want to change OR: click on the course page link to start the QuizPort activity, then click on the "Update this QuizPort" button in the top right of your screen To change a "deadline" on a QuizPort quiz , you log into Moodle as a teacher or admin and do the following: click on the course page link to start the QuizPort activity, the click on the "Edit quizzes" tab. Locate the quiz whose "deadlines" you wish to change and click on the edit icon in the "Edit" column (2nd from the left) It is important to be clear about the difference between the QuizPort activity settings page (also called the QuizPort unit settings page), and a QuizPort quiz settings page. If you understand this difference, I hope that fewer unexpected things will happen in your Moodle course and you will not get so mad best regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Hotpot crossword penalties
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a situation whereby when a student clicks the "Hint" tab while doing a hotpot crossword they seem to be penalised for doing so. For example if there were 10 clues in the crossword and a student got all 10 answers correct but hit the hint button once for each clue (10 times in total) they would get a score of 90% even though they got all the answers correct and should in theory be awarded a score of 100%. How do I ensure that if students get all of the answers correct that they receive a score of 100% even if they used the hint function? I don't see an apply penalties option anywhere.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hotpot crossword penalties
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Frank, I'm afraid Hot Potatoes JCross doesn't have any options for changing the way the scoring works. Although you think that students should not be penalized for getting hints, many teachers, and - more crucially - the creators of Hot Potatoes, do. I personally agree with the penalization of hints, as it prevents students just clicking Hint, Hint, Hint, Hint ... to get all the correct letters of an answer and therefore 100% for each question and then the whole quiz, without having known or throught about a single correct answer. If you would like to give free hints in crosswords, you will need to modify either the html file for the crossword quiz, or the source templates for JCross. locate the html file of your quiz and open it with a text editor locate the "function ShowHint()" function locate the following line within the "ShowHint()" function: `State[CurrGap].HintsAndChecks += 1;` "comment out" the above line, by adding two backslashes, thus: `// State[CurrGap].HintsAndChecks += 1;` save the file and close the text editor That should fix it! Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hotpot crossword penalties
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gordon, That's really useful to me too. And so nice of you to give a technical solution that you don't agree with pedagogically. I think it depends on the kind of students you're working with. I've been lucky enough to mainly work with adults who actually want to learn English - not just get a good score - so it doesn't seem right to penalise them if it's a learning exercise and not a test. Maybe they just don't know the word or maybe they do but need the first letter to find it - I know I sometimes do. I assume it'll work for the other apps and not just JCross? Cheers, Glenys

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hotpot crossword penalties
ResponsesInList.Text: > I assume it'll work for the other apps and not just JCross? Well, something similar will work for all types of Hot Potatoes exercise, although exactly which line of code to modify will probably be slightly different, depending on which app is being changed and the scoring modification that is requried. best regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Overview of 15 Flash video players
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Just reading posts and found nearly every third post has to do with flash audio and video. Some people asked the question "How to play video in HotPotatoes?" And they got it working in HotPotatoes, but found it doesn't work in HotPot in Moodle. Then they changed the player and the code and ... Ta-da, it works!, and blame the previous player. This is because they didn't ask the right question "How to get it working in HotPot/QuizPort in Moodle?" Well it has nothing to do with the player, but the code implementation . (I blogged about what creates the misunderstanding ) There're basically two embed methods: dynamically through javascript with different js libraries and the simple static object tag. The Javscript approach doesn't work in Moodle; the object tag does. So if you prefer your player, don't use js, and turn off the media plugins, as Glenys has advised numerous times here. My aim was to show that (nearly) any player can work in HotPot in Moodle. ( Full overview here ) I put together 15 players on a single page (JCloze) and they play nicely in: (Login as guest should you need to) Moodle 1.9 - HotPot with .htm file Moodle 1.9 - HotPot with .jcl file Moodle 1.9 - QuizPort with .htm file Moodle 1.9 - QuizPort with .jcl file Login to Gordon's Moodle 2 for testing : Moodle 2 - HotPot with .htm file Moodle 2 - HotPot with .jcl file The players are: 9 JW Players ranging from version 1 to 5 3 FlowPlayers: two old ones and the latest version 3.2.7 1 Dew Tube player 1 unknown player 1 generic Flash player My test results of the 15 FLV players with HotPot and QuizPort in Moodle 1.9.11 and Moodle 2, both as .htm and .jcl files in different browsers are on Windows . (note: Opera still requires the click-to-activate for the ActiveX). There's no reason why other browser wouldn't play the video, though, so I'm pretty certain it will be OK, but if you can test on other OS and send me the results, I'd be really thankful. The only one not playing is FlowPlayer in HotPot on Moodle 2. The difficulty is to figure out the absolute url from the Files section, but the real problem I think comes from the way it was developed (in JSON ) so when HotPot escapes the single quotes, things get messy. ( none of a problem since you have it in the install pack with HotPot ) Here's what happens: param name="flashvars" value="config={ " clip " :{ " url " : " absolute-url-to-themovie.flv " , " autoPlay " :false}}&width=300&height=250" Gordon , this is what it shows, if you can fix HotPot escaping the single quotes, I believe we'll get flowplayer working in HotPot Moodle 2 (without the bracket notation) too. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Overview of 15 Flash video players (now with MP4 video)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stan, thanks for the extra info. The file URLs are tricky in Moodle 2.0, firstly because files can be stored all over the place now, and secondly because Moodle has much more control over whether or not a user can access a file. The default is for Moodle to have *complete* control, but you can relax those settings. For a file that is stored within the "Source file" are of a HotPot activity in Moodle 2.0, the URL would look like this: ht t p://myserver.com/moodle /pluginfile.php/ 999 /mod_hotpot/sourcefile/ myfolder/mysoundfile.mp3 The underlined parts will change according to your situation ht t p://myserver.com/moodle the base url of your Moodle site 999 the context id of the HotPot activity. You can discover the context id if you go to the page for editing a HotPot, then roll your cursor over the "Permissions" item in the "Settings" menu (underneath the main Moodle navigation menu) myfolder/mysoundfile.mp3 the path to the file within this HotPot activity's source file area If you file is in the course files area, then you change the URL to something like this: ht t p://myserver.com/moodle /pluginfile.php/ 999 /course/legacy/ myfolder/mysoundfile.mp3 In the above URL, "999" is the course context id. You can discover the course context id by going to the course page and rolling your mouse over the "Permissions" item in the "Users" submenu of the "Settings" menu. I should able to look at the flowplayer on Friday. The info you have kindly supplied will be invaluable. Thank you! regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Background image not showing
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Robert, the first thing I would suggest is to clear the browser caches and "Force-refresh" the page in your browser. But probably you have already done that, so ... THe next thing I would try is to go to one of the computers that is misbehaving and find out what URL it is trying to access for the background image. If the image is within one of the HTML tags, then you can use the browser's "View source" menu option to open the source HTML and find the URL. If the image is defined in a stylesheet (i.e. a ". css " file), then you will need to get the URL of the css file (again, using the browers's "View source" menu option), and then paste the stylesheet's URL into the browser's address bar. Once you have the URL of the background, check it is an absolute URL, then paste it into the address bar of your browser. If it doesn't show, then go to the course files folder of your Moodle site (or whereever the image is stored), navigate to the image file and click on it. The browser should display the image. That's enough for now. Please let me know what happens, and we can take it from there. cheers Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best way to add mp3 to hotpot in moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Barfuss, You're asking a tough question! Adding audio and video in HotPotatoes is not 100% the same as adding audio and video to Moodle or to Moodle through HotPot and through QuizPort, (as Deborah found recently)  i.e. there are some differences that people need to be aware of. We all want to have THE one and only universal method but it's not happening yet. So, the official tutorials ( http://hotpot.uvic.ca/howto/audio.htm ) tell you how to insert a flash player for the Web using their player, or another one. Players, however, don't differ much in that they should basically play the sound by using just the minimum necessary code. I have a small collection of players and the minimum code for each is downloadable (including the player). Here we come to filters. If you want to include sound in Moodle, you can use the Moodle filters and the players that go with Moodle. Moodle uses filters to serve you the sound with a player. The code differs slightly in the URLs. You can tell Moodle not to use filters and use the player you want and the one which you upload . HotPot and QuizPort have 3 or 4 players available and you can use the square bracket notation (if you don't know or don't want to write the player embed code). Or you can tell HotPot and QuizPort to serve your hotpotatoes exercises with your player, in which case you also tell the Module (in the settings) NOT to use the HotPot filter; or you tell the Module to use the Moodle filter. People who tried using javascript to dynamically display the player and the sound found that it's not working, for various reasons. So most of us now go the simple way: inserting an object with the minimal code for their players (without any filters) or the square bracket notatin method provided by HotPot and QuizPort (with the HotPot/QuizPort filters). Hope this clears some of the confusion. (I feel I should offer some examples, though.) Cheers Stan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ang: Re: Best way to add mp3 to hotpot in moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Barfuss, EMBED is ancient and not standard compliant! Don't use it. Your GOOD code is this: 1: Single line without carriage returns in JQuiz! <object type="application/x-shockwave-flash" data="ekstern_mp3_player_1.swf" width="30" height="30"> <param name="movie" value="ekstern_mp3_player_1.swf" /> <param name="FlashVars" value="TheSound= A tuarpusi.mp3&width=30&height=20" /> <param name="loop" value="false" /> <param name="menu" value="false" /> <param name="quality" value="high" /> <param name="bgcolor" value=" #f2ebe3 "> </object> 2: loop, menu, quality are optional and you can safely remove them. 3: file names are case sensitive 4: changed the background colour to yours to blend with the exercise page. 5: mind the quotations. BTW , what does 'atuarpusi' mean? Cheers Stan

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there, I've observed the above behaviour (missing sourcetype). It means there's no file "set to main". It happens when one uploads a file and replaces the already existing one. Although the "Set main file" is selected (appears bold), it (the AJAX ) doesn't refresh.So one ends up with no file sellected as main, hence the error. My solution so far: to re-edit and "set main file" the .jcw, or just choose another file as "main", then go back to "set the main" file again: the original source.(AJAX refreshes then) I don't know if this is Moodle or HotPot causing it. ResponsesInList.Title: transfering data from moodle lessons to quizports
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, Could anyone tell me what the best way to transfer Moodle lesson activities (question pages, in particular) to quizports?  Is there a shorter way of doing it than manually cutting and pasting all those fields (content of question page, answers, grade, etc) into Quizport fields? I have 6 lessons and about 20 question pages per lesson (some have lots of images). Any advice would be much appreciated. Thanks, Katie PS- Can a large amount of text be put into a quizport question field, or should I be looking at a different module?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: transfering data from moodle lessons to quizports
ResponsesInList.Text: As is often the case in Moodle, the "best" way, depends how familiar you are with the tools you have at your disposal. For me, the quickest way would be to extract the information from the Moodle database . If you have access to a database administration program, such as phpMyAdmin , you could extract the lesson pages with something like the following SQL : SELECT title,contents FROM mdl_ lesson_pages WHERE lessonid IN (SELECT id FROM mdl_lesson WHERE course= 99 ) You may need to change "mdl_" to whatever prefix database table prefix your Moodle site is using ("mdl_" is the default). Also, you need to change the "99" to whatever the id is for the course where the lessons are. You could take the above idea a stage further and have the database server create the html too. The following code works on a MySQL server: SELECT CONCAT( '<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Strict//EN"', ' "h t tp://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-strict.dtd">', '<html><head>', '<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8" />', '<title>',title,'</title>', '</head><body>',contents,'</body></html>' ) AS copy_and_paste_to_an_html_file FROM mdl_ lesson_pages WHERE lessonid IN (SELECT id FROM mdl_ lesson WHERE course= 99 ) As before, you will need to change "99", and maybe "mdl_", to suitable values for your Moodle course and database. regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: transfering data from moodle lessons to quizports
ResponsesInList.Text: > Can a large amount of text be put into a quizport question field, > or should I be looking at a different module? QuizPort expects the content and questions to be in files, not fields. The files may be static html files, or they may be interactive quiz files, e.g. Hot Potatoes quizzes. Looked at this way, you question becomes, "Can a large amount of text be put into a file", to which the answer is "Yes". However, of course you need to bear in mind how much you think the students can digest in one page at a time, when they access the information using their favorite browser on their favorite viewing device. regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using jquiz as a test
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jens, I suggest you administer your JQuiz using the QuizPort module (as opposed to the HotPot module) and set the QuizPort output format  to "JQuiz auto-advance" output format. The "JQuiz auto-advance" output format will remove the question navigation buttons, "<=" and "=>", and the numeric progress readout, "1 / 10", and replace them with a progress bar, made up of colored dots, which shows which questions have been completed so far. When one question is finished, the next question will be displayed automatically. regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Newbie to HotPot needs help
ResponsesInList.Text: Stephen, forgive me if you already know this, but there is a difference between a "checkbox" and a "radio button". You seem to be familiar with radio buttons. They are usually round, and occur in a set. Choosing one radio button will un-choose all the others. As a result, you can only have one radio button selected at any one time. JQuiz does not use radio buttons. A checkbox is independent of other checkboxes. For this reason, selecting one checkbox does not un-select any other checkboxes. JQuiz uses checkboxes for "multi-select" questions, When you create a "multi-select" question in JQuiz, the question is displayed using checkboxes. That is to say, each box can be checked or unchecked independently of the others. A multiselect JQuiz question is intended for question such as "Which of the following cities are in Australia?", displayed with a list of cities, some of which are in Australia and some of which are not. If the question you are making only has one correct answer, then you should make the question a "multiple-choice" question, not a "multi-select" question. This will give you the behavior you seem to expect. I have attached an example JQuiz file which contains examples of each of the four types of question that JQuiz offers. Perhaps it will help you understand how the different types of question behave. regards Gordon

ResponsesInList.Text: Stephen, > How do i add something like a "submit answers" button > and then display answers and explainations > after the pupil has completed > eg a random 10 questions out of my bank of 75 questions? There is no need for a "Submit answers" button, because the quiz will detect when all the questions have been correctly answered, and will send the results to Moodle at that point. HotPot quizzes display feedback to each question immediately after that question is attempted. They do not save up the feedback and show it all at the end. If you want all the feedback at the end of the quiz, I suggest you use Moodle's Quiz module. The Quiz module will also alow you to select 10 questions randomly from a question category that contains 75 questions. best regards Gordon

On this forum at least, we use the terms "xml file" and "html file" to differentiate between the two types of source file that the HotPot and QuizPort modules can accept. Note that the each Hot Potatoes application has a unique file extension for the xml files that it can handle: jcl - JCloze jcw - JCross jmt - JMatch jmx - JMix jqz - JQuiz jms - Masher The Hot Potatoes applications, and the QuizPort module, can also recognize Hot Potatoes configuration files: cfg - configuration file FYI , xml is a simple but powerful way to specify data and its structure. You can open any of the above files with a simple text editor and "look" at the contents for youself. Gordon

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stephen, Thanks, appreciation is always motivating! Re: your exercises If you only have text, kids won't be able to know which compound goes on which line. In real life, you'd say "Make a compound from these words" and students will choose a gap on a piece of paper which you can check. Or Randomization: use JQuiz + picture with 'ShortAnswer'. in Configuration/Other/  tick "Show a limited number of questions each time the page loads" (10, for instance). Optional: tick "Shuffle order of questions each time the page loads" Students type in the whole word/compound; the picture is the prompt.
